content:
According to the Financial Times, the latest court documents show that OpenAI is disappointed with the adoption of ChatGPT through Apple Intelligence, claiming that the relevant integration "performed significantly below expectations" since its launch in 2024. Details below.

OpenAI is asking the court to rule before trial

In August 2025, Elon Musk said that X, now merged into SpaceXAI, would sue Apple and OpenAI over an alleged conspiracy to shut out competitors in the field of artificial intelligence. The dispute stems from an agreement between OpenAI and Apple to integrate ChatGPT into Apple Intelligence and Siri.

Since the lawsuit was formally filed, the actual content has gone beyond the App Store ranking issues Musk originally complained about publicly. X and SpaceXAI also accuse Apple of trying to strangle the development of "super apps," including X's plans to turn itself into an "everything app."

In the weeks and months that followed, all the companies involved filed submissions, allegations and defences with the court. Apple and OpenAI have repeatedly argued that their agreement is not exclusive in nature as alleged in the lawsuit; at the same time, court documents have also revealed more details about how this collaboration works behind the scenes.

One such detail was exposed in a filing OpenAI submitted today. As first reported by the Financial Times, OpenAI "said it was disappointed with the interest generated by Apple for iPhone users," with the two companies having reached an agreement as early as 2024 to have ChatGPT provide the technology for "Apple Intelligence."

The report states as follows:

Court documents on Wednesday indicated that when the 2024 agreement was reached, OpenAI had expected to generate a "halo effect" through Apple's promotion and brand tie-up, and to attract more subscriptions from Apple Intelligence users. However, one month after the ChatGPT integration was rolled out, performance "appeared to get off to a slow start," and OpenAI immediately lowered its forecast for the number of weekly active users. By the summer of 2025, "it had become quite clear that Apple's integration of ChatGPT was performing significantly below expectations."

The report notes that today's legal filings contain several redacted passages of dialogue, but the unredacted portions show that senior executives at OpenAI feared Apple might "want to move faster" to find another AI partner.

When Apple Intelligence was first unveiled in 2024, Craig Federighi said in an interview that Apple ultimately wanted to let users choose between different AI models, specifically mentioning Google Gemini as a potential future integration option.

Although that particular partnership did not ultimately materialise, Apple later switched to Google's Gemini model to provide the technology for the all-new Siri AI, while Xcode has also expanded support for coding agent tools from Anthropic, Google and OpenAI.

Returning to today's court filings, the Financial Times notes that the documents also suggest that the way Apple rolled out ChatGPT may be one reason for the low adoption rate, since the relevant integration feature is off by default.

Finally, according to Reuters, OpenAI also argues that SpaceX's recent securities filings are sufficient to undermine SpaceXAI's allegations that its partnership with Apple harmed market competition. OpenAI stated in its filing that SpaceX's IPO registration statement is full of disclosures that are "the exact opposite of the competitive harm alleged in the lawsuit."

On these grounds, OpenAI is asking Judge Mark Pittman to rule in its favour on SpaceXAI's antitrust claims before trial. The case is currently scheduled to go to trial in January.
